title: Jade Star Ampalaya (Jade Star F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Jade Star ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety from East West Seed. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Jade Star ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Jade Star F1 or Jade Star L. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed.

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Jade Star ampalaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Jade Star F1 or Jade Star L, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 48 to 57 days after transplanting (Jade Star L). No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 48 to 57 days after transplanting (Jade Star L).
**Fruit:** Green, cylindrical with a slightly blunt tip.
Bred for downy mildew resistance (East West history page).
Flowered later than Galaxy, Galactica and Bonito in a 2013 La Union trial, with similar marketable yield.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: East West's first hybrid, which the company calls the first commercial vegetable hybrid bred in the Philippines, still in the ampalaya variety table and used as an entry in DMMMSU trials. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Jade Star ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Jade Star F1 the same as Jade Star?
items.a: Yes. Jade Star F1 is another name for Jade Star. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Jade Star?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
